overview: This bill gives commissioned officers of the U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps, a uniformed service of public health professionals such as doctors and nurses who work in federal health agencies, the same leave rights as members of the Armed Forces. It does this by applying the military's leave rules, which cover things like vacation, parental and other types of leave, to Public Health Service officers and their beneficiaries, and repealing a separate, older leave provision for the Corps. The Senate passed it on October 9, 2025, and as of October 17, 2025, it was being held at the desk in the House awaiting action.
for: Supporters say Public Health Service officers serve under military-style rules and deploy in emergencies, so they should get the same leave benefits as the other uniformed services.
against: Critics say the bill changes benefits without stating their cost, and that tying the Corps to military leave rules means future military leave changes would automatically apply to it.
